subject: Business
title: Just-in-Time Inventory
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Just-in-Time Inventory.

hook.text: Toyota keeps only two hours of parts on the factory floor. If a delivery is late, the entire line stops.

buildup.text: Just-in-time (JIT) means ordering materials to arrive exactly when needed — no sooner, no later.

discovery.text: JIT eliminates storage costs, reduces waste, and forces suppliers to be perfectly reliable.

twist.text: JIT has zero buffer. A single disruption — a storm, a strike, a pandemic — halts everything downstream.

climax.text: The 2021 chip shortage shut down car factories globally because automakers had no inventory buffer for semiconductors.

punchline.text: Just-in-time is efficient in calm waters. Just-in-case saves you in storms.

quiz.question: What is the biggest risk of just-in-time inventory?
options: Any single disruption can halt the entire production line
It requires too much warehouse space
Suppliers always overcharge for JIT deliveries

details.summary: Just-in-time inventory is a strategy where materials arrive precisely when needed for production, minimizing storage costs and waste. Pioneered by Toyota, JIT requires reliable suppliers, accurate demand forecasting, and seamless coordination across the supply chain.
details.whyItMatters: JIT revolutionized manufacturing efficiency by eliminating costly warehousing of excess inventory. However, the COVID-19 pandemic exposed its vulnerability to disruption, sparking renewed debate about balancing efficiency with resilience.
takeaways: Materials arrive exactly when needed, minimizing inventory holding costs
Toyota pioneered JIT as part of the Toyota Production System
JIT depends on reliable suppliers and is vulnerable to supply disruptions

faq.question: What are the main advantages of just-in-time inventory?
faq.answer: Reduced warehouse space and holding costs, less capital tied up in inventory, decreased waste from obsolete or expired stock, faster identification of quality defects, and improved cash flow since materials are paid for closer to when revenue is generated.

faq.question: Why did the pandemic expose weaknesses in just-in-time systems?
faq.answer: JIT depends on predictable demand and reliable supply. COVID-19 disrupted both simultaneously through factory shutdowns, shipping delays, and demand volatility. Companies with minimal buffer stock faced immediate shortages and production halts.
